notes: raw_row is a SYNTHETIC row in the storage/sources/whatsapp.jsonl ledger-row shape (every id, name, timestamp and text in it is invented) — a 1:1 INBOUND message (session_type=0, @lid linked-id, is_from_me=0). It is the WU-N3 1:1 PARTNER-NAME GAP case: ZWACHATSESSION.ZPARTNERNAME for this jid is only a formatted phone string (UNresolved), so the old 1:1 branch produced sender.name=null; the FIX adds a ZWAPROFILEPUSHNAME[from_jid] fallback, recovering the partner's self-set push name 'Jordan'. The expected_envelope below is the AFTER-FIX projection (adapter called with opts.pushByJid = {'100555010000001@lid':'Jordan'}). NOTE: the row deliberately carries NO sender_jid/sender_name/session_label/member_jid keys (the shape of rows written before the connector forward stamp) — the adapter tolerates their absence and resolves the sender externally. Capabilities are all FALSE (the maximally-degraded platform): ZPARENTMESSAGE always null (reply_to_available=false); mentions are text-embedded @<digits> with no structured field (structured_mentions=false); self-jid is @lid-masked (self_identity_reliable=false); no To/Cc envelope (addressing_first_class=false). Because the platform cannot tell, every directed_at_me_signals.* is false. The raw row stamps an ISO ts; the adapter converts to integer ms — expected_envelope.ts is the integer. reply_to_id is ABSENT on THIS row because this row has no reply target. The blanket claim that 'WhatsApp never stores a reply target' was FALSE and is removed: ZPARENTMESSAGE carries it on 2 store rows, and the contextInfo protobuf in ZWAMEDIAITEM.ZMETADATA carries it on hundreds more. capabilities.reply_to_available=false below is therefore a CARRIED DEFECT, not a platform fact -- it reflects what the adapter currently reads, and it is tracked as its own node.
